title: 📰 AI news · October 27

items.title: Stolen GitHub tokens pull secrets out of projects
items.text: Wiz found a campaign called Gheist: with a stolen token, attackers add a job to a project that prints all its secrets into the run log. If your bot or site lives on GitHub, your access keys sit in those secrets. Check which secrets are stored in your projects and what rights your tokens have. Free guide "Protecting your computer, code and access" — send the word "protect" to the bot.

items.title: An AI tool helped breach more than 90 organizations
items.text: South Korean police named seven suspects who used ARTEX AI, a program that finds weak spots by itself, and stole 8.2 million records. If you run a bot, site or AI agent, such programs look for a way in at small projects too. Check which keys and access points your system exposes to the outside.

items.title: Spyware in fake Telegram copies takes your two-step password
items.text: Modified copies of Telegram and WeChat that people install by hand capture the two-step verification password and can change the phone number or delete the account. If your Telegram is tied to a channel or bot, losing it affects them too. Check that your messenger comes from the official store.

items.title: DreamHost forced email and FTP password resets
items.text: After File Manager outages, the host blocked access until users updated email and FTP passwords. If your site runs on a host, file and email access sits in these places. Check which passwords and mail forwarding rules are set on your hosting.

items.title: Malicious code found in 953 online stores
items.text: Sansec found a script in Magento stores that shows harmful code to real shoppers and a clean page to security scanners. If you run a store, your customers' data passes through that page. Check which third-party scripts are connected to your site.

items.title: GPT-6.1 Terra: three times faster, half the price
items.text: OpenAI released a model for coding and computer use. It costs $1 per million input tokens and $5 per million output, 50% below GPT-6.1 Sol. The error rate fell from 53.6% to 16.7%.

items.title: Six patterns that make AI text tiring to read
items.text: Researchers at NYU and UT Austin compared 14 models with human writing. Small models came closest to people, and Claude Opus 5.5 beat Opus 5 in 19 of 21 comparisons.

items.title: Instagram tests videos up to 90 minutes
items.text: The new upload type is called Features. A tool called Clips as Reels turns a long video into a Reel with a link to the full version. The test runs with creators in Brazil and the US.

items.title: Apple unveils an iPad mini with an OLED screen
items.text: 8.5-inch display, A20 Pro chip, speakers under the glass. Price starts at $699, pre-orders open October 28.

items.title: Toyota puts $6.4 billion a year into robots
items.text: According to the Financial Times, the plan is 400,000 robots, first in its own factories. Goldman Sachs says Toyota could take 3 to 8% of the humanoid robot market by 2035.

takeaway: Several of today's stories are about access: GitHub tokens, hosting passwords, two-step protection in Telegram. Through them attackers reach projects and accounts. Recommendation: check where your bot's keys are stored and what rights your GitHub tokens have.
